key_path: Sign up at slack.com/get-started with email (6-digit confirmation code) or Google/Apple OAuth
Create a workspace (name, first channel) - or join an existing one
Go to api.slack.com/apps > Create New App > From manifest (agent can write the YAML/JSON manifest with scopes)
Install to Workspace (OAuth consent; on managed workspaces this becomes an admin approval request)
Copy Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-) or User Token (xoxp-) from OAuth & Permissions
human_gates_notes: Admin approval of apps/MCP clients when app approval is on (common in paid workspaces). Slack CLI login requires pasting a /slackauthticket command into Slack - a human step.

agent_native_auth.cli_device_login: partial - Slack CLI 'slack login' issues an auth ticket the human pastes into Slack
agent_native_auth.mcp_oauth_dcr: no - docs: 'We do not support SSE-based connections or Dynamic Client Registration'; app must be Marketplace-published or internal
agent_native_auth.management_api_mints_keys: yes - App Manifest API (apps.manifest.create) with app configuration tokens can create apps programmatically
agent_native_auth.free_tier_or_sandbox: yes - free workspace; developer sandboxes via Developer Program

remote.auth: confidential OAuth with registered app client_id/secret (PKCE now supported for desktop); user token scopes

mcp.one_click_install: via partner clients only: Claude.ai, Claude Code, Cursor, Perplexity
mcp.chatgpt_directory: not listed in Slack's partner list

docs_for_agents.markdown_pages: yes - append .md to any docs.slack.dev URL; llms-sitemap.md index
docs_for_agents.openapi: legacy community spec only (slackapi/slack-api-specs, not maintained)

score_justification: Best-in-class docs for LLMs and manifest-driven app creation, but tokens require an app install and MCP is locked to directory/internal apps with no DCR.
best_practice: Language-split llms-full files (platform + JS/Python/Java/Deno) so agents load only the SDK they need.
biggest_gap: No personal token and no DCR: every agent needs a registered Slack app (and often admin approval) before it can touch the API or MCP.
